doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Choosing I May Be Wrong as his theme song
summary: The theme was picked casually for the Apollo and stuck for fifty years.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: There was also no theme song established at that time until you established one.
Yeah. [sings] I May Be Wrong and . . . yes.
I don’t know, just picked a tune, you know, something we liked, and that was it. As a matter of fact, I think that’s something I’ve never recorded. Have I?
Not a bad one to put on the list.
That’s right. We’ll have to put it on the list.
But was that like a spur-of-the-moment thing, because did your band have a theme song of its own?
Yeah, we just did something, and we picked that out. Maybe somebody in the orchestra suggested it, but just exactly how it came about, I don’t know.
And then it stuck for fifty years. [laughter]
It was a good choice, then.
